BRAIN MRI: 3/15/2023 10:45 AM

CLINICAL HISTORY: 62-year-old man with history of grade 2 right
frontal pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma with initial resection
2001 status post re-resection 5/20/2015, 11/30/2018 for recurrent
tumor showing grade 2 pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma. Clinically
stable. Surveillance imaging.

COMPARISON: Brain MRI 9/18/2022.

TECHNIQUE: 3-D sagittal FLAIR, axial diffusion, axial T1
pre-gadolinium, axial and coronal T1 postgadolinium, and axial
perfusion sequences were performed on at 3.0 Tesla.

FINDINGS:

Status post right frontoparietal craniotomy with
underlying resection cavity centered on the right superior
frontal lobe extending deep to the subependymal region of the
right trigone with no significant change in cystic
encephalomalacia surrounding resection cavity. Evaluation is
partially limited by metallic susceptibility artifact within the
medial aspect resection cavity.

Compared with 9/18/2022, no significant interval change in
minimal nodular enhancement along the right tentorial incisura at
the deep medial aspect of resection cavity adjacent to the region
of magnetic susceptibility. No significant interval change in
confluent FLAIR signal hyperintensity predominantly involving the
subcortical white matter of the right frontal lobe which extends
deep to the periventricular white matter. Scattered additional
foci of FLAIR signal hyperintensity in the periventricular and
deep supratentorial white matter are unchanged and nonspecific,
possibly representing sequelae of prior treatment or senescent
microvascular change. No reduced diffusion to suggest acute
infarct or cytotoxic edema.

Ventricles and sulci are unchanged in size with stable ex vacuo
dilatation of the right lateral ventricle and trigone. Small T1
hypointense tract extending via the left middle frontal gyrus
and anterior corpus callosum to the left lateral ventricle with
minimal magnetic susceptibility consistent with blood products,
likely reflecting prior ventricular drainage catheter tract.

No pathologic extra-axial collection.

IMPRESSION:

Compared with 9/18/2022, no evidence of disease progression.
Cystic encephalomalacia and surrounding gliosis involving the
right frontal resection cavity with unchanged minimal nodular
dural enhancement at the deep medial aspect of the surgical
cavity.
